question: Can a larger native Metal prefill block improve time to first token on the released arithmetic K2 checkpoint while preserving full-history greedy outputs?
protocol: Use exact prefixes of the frozen 131072-token ledger (the engineering workload need not end in a question). Keep identical weights, BF16, full-history KV, prompt IDs, greedy decoding, output cap, cache limit and native MLX. Warm each block with 1024 tokens. For both lengths use balanced AB/BA crossovers, two synchronized observations per implementation. Compare all emitted IDs, full last-position vocabulary logits along each decoded path, median TTFT and peak allocation. Test only the prespecified block sizes.
decision: At each length require all output IDs identical on all observations, maximum per-step relative logit RMS <=0.005, treatment median TTFT <=0.90 times baseline and peak <=baseline+0.30 GiB. If either length fails close 128K performance promotion and retain current default. A passing pilot permits one independent full 131072-token original request against its measured 128-token reference with 22 identical emitted IDs, >=10% TTFT improvement and <=0.30 GiB increase.
